learning_objectives.title: Central Ideas and Details
learning_objectives.statement: Students will determine the central idea of a text and/or interpret the key details supporting that idea.
include: Students will determine the central idea of a text and/or interpret the key details supporting that idea.

learning_objectives.title: Command of Evidence
learning_objectives.statement: Students will determine the evidence in a text that best supports a specified claim or point.
include: Students will determine the evidence in a text that best supports a specified claim or point.
Textual: Students will determine the textual evidence (e.g., a fact, detail, or example from a text) that best supports a specified claim or point.
Quantitative: Students will determine the quantitative evidence (i.e., data from an informational graphic) that best supports a specified claim or point.

learning_objectives.title: Inferences
learning_objectives.statement: Students will draw reasonable inferences based on explicit and/or implicit information and ideas in a text.
include: Students will draw reasonable inferences based on explicit and/or implicit information and ideas in a text.

learning_objectives.title: Words in Context
learning_objectives.statement: Students will determine the meaning of a high-utility academic word or phrase in context or use such vocabulary in a contextually appropriate way.
include: Students will determine the meaning of a high-utility academic word or phrase in context or use such vocabulary in a contextually appropriate way.

learning_objectives.title: Text Structure and Purpose
learning_objectives.statement: Students will analyze the structure of a text or determine the main rhetorical purpose of a text.
include: Students will analyze the structure of a text or determine the main rhetorical purpose of a text.

learning_objectives.title: Cross-Text Connections
learning_objectives.statement: Students will draw reasonable connections between two texts on related topics.
include: Students will draw reasonable connections between two texts on related topics.

learning_objectives.title: Rhetorical Synthesis
learning_objectives.statement: Students will strategically integrate information and ideas on a topic to form an effective sentence achieving a specified rhetorical aim.
include: Students will strategically integrate information and ideas on a topic to form an effective sentence achieving a specified rhetorical aim.

learning_objectives.title: Transitions
learning_objectives.statement: Students will determine the most effective transition word or phrase to logically connect information and ideas in a text.
include: Students will determine the most effective transition word or phrase to logically connect information and ideas in a text.

learning_objectives.title: Boundaries
learning_objectives.statement: Students will edit text to ensure that sentences are conventionally complete.
include: Students will edit text to ensure that sentences are conventionally complete.
Between Sentences: Students will use contextually appropriate punctuation to properly mark the end of a sentence.

Within Sentences: Students will coordinate clauses within a sentence or elements in a series using appropriate punctuation and, in some cases, a conjunction or conjunctive adverb; incorporate supplementary information (e.g., appositives, parentheticals) using appropriate punctuation; and recognize circumstances in which no punctuation is needed to set off sentence elements.

learning_objectives.title: Form, Structure, and Sense
learning_objectives.statement: Students will edit text to conform to conventional usage.
include: Students will edit text to conform to conventional usage.
Subject-Verb Agreement: Students will ensure agreement in number between a subject and a verb.
Pronoun-Antecedent Agreement: Students will ensure agreement in number between a pronoun and its antecedent.
Verb Finiteness: Students will use verbs and verbals (i.e., gerunds, participles, infinitives) in contextually appropriate ways.
Verb Tense and Aspect: Students will use contextually appropriate tenses and aspects of verbs.
Subject-Modifier Placement: Students will place modifying elements in sentences (e.g., participles) in contextually appropriate ways.

Genitives and Plurals: Students will make contextually appropriate choices among singular, plural, singular possessive, and plural possessive nouns and pronouns and among possessive determiners (its, their, your), contractions (it’s, they’re, you’re), and adverbs (there).

learning_objectives.statement: Questions will require students to solve problems by using a proportional relationship between quantities, calculating or using a ratio or rate, and/or using units, derived units, and unit conversion.
include: Questions will require students to solve problems by using a proportional relationship between quantities, calculating or using a ratio or rate, and/or using units, derived units, and unit conversion.
Apply proportional relationships, ratios, and rates in a wide variety of contexts. Examples include, but are not limited to, scale drawings and problems in the natural and social sciences.
Solve problems involving derived units, including those that arise from products (e.g., kilowatt-hours) and quotients (e.g., population per square kilometer).
Solve problems involving: a one-step unit conversion. a multistep or multidimensional unit conversion.
Understand and use the fact that when two quantities are in a proportional relationship, if one changes by a scale factor, then the other also changes by the same scale factor.

learning_objectives.title: Percentages
learning_objectives.statement: Use percentages to solve problems in a variety of contexts: including, but not limited to, discounts, interest, taxes, and tips.
include: Use percentages to solve problems in a variety of contexts: including, but not limited to, discounts, interest, taxes, and tips.
Use percentages to solve problems in a variety of contexts: including those that involve percent increases and decreases for many different quantities.
Understand and use the relationship between percent change and growth factor (5% and 1.05, for example); include percentages greater than or equal to 100%.

learning_objectives.title: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread
learning_objectives.statement: Analyze and interpret numerical data distributions represented with frequency tables, histograms, dot plots, and box plots.
include: Analyze and interpret numerical data distributions represented with frequency tables, histograms, dot plots, and box plots.
For quantitative variables, calculate, compare, and interpret mean, median, and range.
Compare distributions using measures of center and spread, including distributions with different means and the same standard deviations.
Understand and describe the effect of outliers on mean and median.
exclude: Compare distributions using measures of center and spread, including: distributions with different standard deviations. (SAT and PSAT/NMSQT only, not PSAT 8/9)

learning_objectives.title: Two-variable data: Models and scatterplots
learning_objectives.statement: Analyze and interpret data represented in a scatterplot, but do not make predictions.
include: Analyze and interpret data represented in a scatterplot, but do not make predictions.
Fit linear models to data represented in a scatterplot.
Given a relationship between two quantities, read and interpret graphs modeling the relationship.
exclude: Analyze and interpret data represented in a scatterplot to make predictions. (SAT and PSAT/NMSQT only, not PSAT 8/9)
Fit quadratic and exponential models to data represented in a scatterplot. (SAT and PSAT/NMSQT only, not PSAT 8/9)
Compare linear and exponential growth. (SAT and PSAT/NMSQT only, not PSAT 8/9)

learning_objectives.title: Probability and conditional probability
learning_objectives.statement: Use one- and two-way tables, area models, and other representations to find relative frequency, probabilities, and conditional probabilities. Calculate, express, or interpret the probability or conditional probability of an event using a data display showing frequencies for a single variable, a two-way table, an area model, or a description of a situation. Infrequently, given a probability, determine an unknown number in a data display showing frequencies for a single variable, a two-way table, or a description of a situation, including using a probability to determine the frequency of an event.
include: Use one- and two-way tables, area models, and other representations to find relative frequency, probabilities, and conditional probabilities. Calculate, express, or interpret the probability or conditional probability of an event using a data display showing frequencies for a single variable, a two-way table, an area model, or a description of a situation. Infrequently, given a probability, determine an unknown number in a data display showing frequencies for a single variable, a two-way table, or a description of a situation, including using a probability to determine the frequency of an event.

learning_objectives.title: Area and volume
learning_objectives.statement: Solve real-world and mathematical problems about the: area or perimeter of a geometric figure or an object that can be modeled by a geometric figure using given information.
include: Solve real-world and mathematical problems about the: area or perimeter of a geometric figure or an object that can be modeled by a geometric figure using given information.

Solve real-world and mathematical problems about the: surface area or volume of a geometric figure or an object that can be modeled by a geometric figure using given information such as length, area, surface area, or volume.
Apply knowledge that changing by a scale factor of k changes all lengths by a factor of k, changes all areas by a factor of k^2, and changes all volumes by a factor of k^3.
Demonstrate procedural fluency by selecting the correct: area formula and correctly calculating a specified value.
Demonstrate procedural fluency by selecting the correct: surface area or volume formula and correctly calculating a specified value.

learning_objectives.title: Lines, angles, and triangles
learning_objectives.statement: Know and directly apply the triangle angle sum theorem.
include: Know and directly apply the triangle angle sum theorem.
exclude: Use concepts and theorems relating to congruence and similarity of triangles to solve problems. (SAT and PSAT/NMSQT only, not PSAT 8/9)
Determine which statements may be required to prove certain relationships or to satisfy a given theorem. (SAT and PSAT/NMSQT only, not PSAT 8/9)
Apply knowledge that changing by a scale factor of k changes all lengths by a factor of k, but angle measures remain unchanged. (SAT and PSAT/NMSQT only, not PSAT 8/9)
Know and directly apply relevant theorems such as the: triangle angle sum theorem. (SAT and PSAT/NMSQT only, not PSAT 8/9)
Know and directly apply relevant theorems such as the: vertical angle theorem and the relationship of angles formed when a transversal cuts parallel lines. (SAT and PSAT/NMSQT only, not PSAT 8/9)

learning_objectives.title: Right triangles and trigonometry
learning_objectives.statement: Solve problems in a variety of contexts using the Pythagorean theorem.
include: Solve problems in a variety of contexts using the Pythagorean theorem.
exclude: Solve problems in a variety of contexts using: properties of special right triangles. (SAT and PSAT/NMSQT only, not PSAT 8/9)
Solve problems in a variety of contexts using: right triangle trigonometry. (SAT and PSAT/NMSQT only, not PSAT 8/9)
Use similarity to calculate values of sine, cosine, and tangent. (SAT and PSAT/NMSQT only, not PSAT 8/9)
Solve problems using the relationship between sine and cosine of complementary angles. (SAT and PSAT/NMSQT only, not PSAT 8/9)

learning_objectives.title: SAT skills not assessed on the PSAT 8/9
learning_objectives.statement: These skills are assessed on the SAT and PSAT/NMSQT but not on the PSAT 8/9.
exclude: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error (SAT and PSAT/NMSQT only, not PSAT 8/9)
Evaluating statistical claims: Observational studies and experiments (SAT and PSAT/NMSQT only, not PSAT 8/9)
Circles (SAT and PSAT/NMSQT only, not PSAT 8/9)
